Thomas Paine (born Thomas Pain , [ 1 ] February 9, 1737 [ O.S. January 29, 1736] [ Note 1 ] – June 8, 1809; / ˈ t ɒ m ə s ˈ p eɪ n / ) was an English-born American Founding Father , inventor, political philosopher , and statesman. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] His pamphlets Common Sense (1776) and The American Crisis (1776–1783) framed the Patriot argument for independence from Great Britain at the outset of the American Revolution . [ 4 ] Paine advanced Enlightenment-era arguments for human rights that shaped revolutionary discourse on both sides of the Atlantic. [ 5 ]
